questions.question: The Brundtland definition of sustainable development is development that:
options: Meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Maximises GDP growth in every year
Bans all use of natural resources
Prioritises the environment over jobs in all cases

questions.question: A factory's effluent kills fish and sickens downstream users who get no compensation. Economically this is:
options: A negative externality — real costs landing on people outside the factory's transactions, so private cost sits below social cost

questions.question: Clean air is a public good because it is:
options: Non-excludable and non-rival — nobody can be fenced out, and one person's breathing does not use up another's

questions.question: The tragedy of the commons predicts that an ownerless fish stock will be:
options: Raced to exhaustion — each fisher correctly reasons that a spared fish will simply be caught by someone else

questions.question: South Africa is DOUBLY exposed to climate change because:
options: Its coal-heavy economy is among the world's most carbon-intensive, AND the region is warming at nearly twice the global average
It has no renewable resources and no coastline

questions.question: South Africa's water situation is precarious because:
options: Rainfall is double the world average but polluted
Rainfall is about half the world average, while rivers carry acid mine drainage, sewage from failing works and farm runoff

questions.question: Biodiversity is described as economic capital because:
options: It is the genetic library for medicine and crops, and the asset base of the tourism industry

questions.question: The economic reading of environmental damage is that it is:
options: A moral issue with no economic content
A cost only to rich countries
Future GDP quietly draining away — lost harvests, deterred tourists, sickened workers, rebuilt cities

subtopics.title: Making Sustainability Pay: the Policy Toolkit

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY command-and-control measures?
options: Emission standards, environmental impact assessments, fishing quotas, water-use licences
Carbon tax, plastic-bag levy, tyre levy

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax, in force since 2019:
options: Prices each ton of carbon dioxide, making the social cost private so every producer saves by polluting less — Africa's first such tax

questions.question: Tradable permits work by:
options: Letting each firm choose its own cap
Fixing prices and letting pollution vary freely
Capping total pollution and letting firms trade allowances — the cap secures the outcome, trading finds the cheapest cutters

questions.question: Community ownership of conservancies cures a commons problem because:
options: It removes wildlife from the economy
Wildlife becomes a village asset with a defending owner instead of a poaching target owned by nobody

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 matters as:
options: The most successful environmental treaty — CFCs phased out, the ozone layer healing — proof that cooperation can work
The treaty that created carbon markets
A failed attempt to ban coal

questions.question: The Rio Earth Summit of 1992 produced:
options: The Kyoto targets and the Paris rulebook
Agenda 21, the Convention on Biological Diversity, and the UNFCCC with its common-but-differentiated-responsibilities principle

questions.question: Paris 2015 differs from Kyoto 1997 in that Paris is:
options: Universal but voluntary — every nation sets its own progressively tightened contributions, aiming well below two degrees
An agreement between the US and China alone

questions.question: South Africa's Just Energy Transition Partnership involves:
options: The IMF lending for new coal stations
A ban on all mining by 2030
Wealthy nations pledging 8,5 billion dollars to help decarbonise without abandoning coal workers and coal towns

questions.question: The factory's books look excellent while the village suffers because:
options: The biggest cost of production — medicine, lost catches, boiled water — lands outside the factory's fence and appears in nobody's invoice

questions.question: Nobody dumps sludge in their own yard, yet the river gets dumped in, because:
options: The yard has a defending owner and the river has no owner to send the bill — what everybody owns, nobody protects
Dumping in rivers is legal everywhere

questions.question: The village never hires the anti-dumping truck because:
options: Clean air cannot be fenced to paying customers, so everyone free-rides and waits for someone else to pay

questions.question: The one-line diagnosis of market-driven environmental damage:
options: The damage is priced at zero — the market cannot count a cost that carries no price tag

questions.question: The four price tags, in the lesson's order, are:
options: The rule, the tax, the reward, the owner
The ban, the bribe, the border, the bailout
The fine, the subsidy, the quota, the treaty
The inspector, the accountant, the chief, the judge

questions.question: A pollution tax 'polices itself' because:
options: Every litre not dumped is money kept — the factory's own accountant now watches the pipe all year round

questions.question: The weakness of a pure rule-based approach is that:
options: The inspector must keep coming, and a firm that could clean up cheaply has no reason to beat the minimum

questions.question: 'A springbok that pays the village's school fees is guarded' illustrates:
options: Property rights curing the commons — ownership gives the community the right to charge and the reason to protect

questions.question: Climate negotiation is 'the hardest free-rider problem on earth' because:
options: Every country's pipe empties into the same atmosphere, and each is tempted to let the others cut first
The atmosphere belongs to the UN

questions.question: Kyoto's design lesson was that:
options: Strict homework for the rich only — with the biggest polluter unsigned and fast growers exempt — barely moves a global curve

questions.question: The recent COP additions worth naming are:
options: The end of all fossil fuel use by 2025
A coal phase-down pledge, a loss and damage fund, and a global stocktake calling for transition away from fossil fuels
The cancellation of the Paris Agreement

questions.question: A JUST transition for a coal town means:
options: Retraining workers, bringing new industries, and keeping the lights on while the grid greens — the social leg of sustainability
